html:
Maria Theresa ruled the Habsburg lands from 1740 to 1780, the only woman to do so. She inherited them at 23 under a law her father had made to let her succeed.

At once Prussia's Frederick the Great seized Silesia, and in the War of the Austrian Succession several powers tried to divide her lands. She kept most of them, with Hungarian help, but lost Silesia for good. Her husband Francis Stephen became Holy Roman Emperor.

She reformed the state: a central government, a standing army, tax on nobles' lands, and in 1774 schooling for all children. She had sixteen children, among them the emperor Joseph II and Marie Antoinette, queen of France. Her reign made Vienna a centre of music for Haydn and Mozart. See Austria.
